reflection.text:

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean profile, unanimous 1-NN atlas vote across activating doses.

## Unblinding

Compound: **proteasome inhibitor I** (PubChem CID [16760625](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/16760625))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Protein degradation**, BBBC021 annotates **Protein degradation**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (4/4). The Scientist's own call was **Protein degradation** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

The call was correct because I prioritized the unanimous 4/4 NSC atlas vote for Protein degradation across 0.1, 1, 3 and 10 uM over the split k-neighbour tallies. The early acquisition choice at 1 uM captured the discriminating nuclear signature of high eccentricity (z=+11.8) with reduced DNA mean (z=-7.6), and bridging wells at 3 uM and 0.1 uM showed it persisted early (eccentricity z=+10.5 and +8.7), which fit proteasome inhibition better than mitotic arrest.

What misled me was the very strong tubulin signal at 10 uM with tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4 and tub_mean z=+11.3, plus dose-response rho=+1.00 for tub_mean. The describe_phenotype visual candidate of Microtubule stabilizers and the first compare_to_reference_atlas k-NN split of Protein degradation 3/10 versus Microtubule stabilizers 3/10 kept stabilizers at 0.20-0.25 and capped final confidence at 0.55.

In retrospect the tubulin brightening was a dose-continuous co-phenotype, not evidence against degradation, and the low-DNA nuclear enlargement should have been weighted more against DNA damage and Eg5 alternatives. Keeping the stabilizer alternative was reasonable, but the unanimous per-well NSC was the right tie-breaker.

What was right:
- Followed unanimous 4/4 NSC vote for Protein degradation across 0.1, 1, 3, 10 uM despite split k-NN.
- Recognized early-onset nuclear elongation with low DNA intensity (nuc_eccentricity z=+11.8 at 1 uM and +8.7 at 0.1 uM, nuc_dna_mean ~-7) as proteasome-related rather than mitotic.
- Used bridging acquisitions at 3 uM and 0.1 uM plus dose-response for tub_mean (rho=+1.00) to show tubulin effect was dose-continuous co-phenotype.

What was wrong or missed:
- Over-weighted 10 uM tubulin surge (tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4, tub_mean z=+11.3) and microscopist Microtubule stabilizers candidate, keeping stabilizers at 0.20.
- Treated split k-NN (Microtubule stabilizers 3/10, DNA damage 2-3/10, Eg5 3/10) as viable alternatives despite unanimous NSC.
- Left DNA damage/DNA replication hypotheses open on basis of nuc_dna_mean decrease without a cell-cycle or DNA-damage counter-measurement during the run.

Proposed next experiment: Measure chymotrypsin-like proteasome activity with fluorogenic substrate plus ubiquitin-conjugate western blot across 0.1-10 uM versus a reference proteasome inhibitor, with parallel in vitro tubulin polymerization assay to test whether the dose-dependent tubulin brightening is direct stabilization or secondary protein accumulation.

- PMID [16862585](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16862585/): Proteasome inhibition and Parkinson's disease modeling. *Ann Neurol* (2006) — Proteasome inhibition has been studied experimentally in Parkinson's disease modeling.
- PMID [19606213](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19606213/): Synergy between proteasome inhibitors and imatinib mesylate in chronic myeloid leukemia. *PLoS One* (2009) — Proteasome inhibitors have been studied in combination with imatinib in chronic myeloid leukemia models.
